data.name: CalibrationSimulateHint
data.value: Trace your palm or enter its dimensions. Write with a mouse or a few contacts. Enough contacts pressed within the time window and clustered within the traced palm bounds automatically erase, without contact-area reports.

data.name: CalibrationSimulationOnly
data.value: Traced dimensions set eraser size; contact count, timing and spatial bounds trigger erasing. Decisions persist until lift-off. Save and apply to use these settings when annotating.

data.name: CalibrationDescription
data.value: Trace your palm, collect repeated presses, and try writing and erasing on a separate canvas. Settings change only when applied.

data.name: CalibrationClearConfirm
data.value: Clear calibration and restore the legacy touch policy?

data.name: CalibrationNone
data.value: Not calibrated. Using the legacy touch policy.

data.name: CalibrationSaved
data.value: Calibrated. Applied only to the matching display, DPI, and input source.

data.name: CalibrationMismatch
data.value: Display settings do not match. Recalibrate on the display you use.

data.name: CalibrationOutlineHint
data.value: Remove your palm, then trace its outline with a mouse or pen, or enter width and height in DIPs. Maximize the window for a larger capture area.

data.name: CalibrationPressHint
data.value: Press inside the area below, hold briefly, then lift. Repeat at least three times. Only one contact box is accepted per press; canceled presses or contacts leaving the area do not count.

data.name: CalibrationNibHint
data.value: Optional: press three times with a passive nib that reports contact dimensions. Skip active pens that report pressure only; skipping preserves the old nib threshold.

data.name: CalibrationPreviewHint
data.value: Write with a mouse, pen, or finger and erase with your palm. This canvas is separate from your page. Size adjustments do not change the recognition threshold.

data.name: CalibrationReady
data.value: Waiting for input. The first press locks the input source and display environment.

data.name: CalibrationEnvironmentChanged
data.value: Display or DPI changed. Collection was interrupted. Please resample.

data.name: CalibrationMultipleContacts
data.value: Multiple contact boxes detected; this press was discarded. The device must report a single palm box. Separate finger areas cannot be added together.

data.name: CalibrationNoArea
data.value: No valid contact dimensions. Pressure alone cannot calibrate area. Check hardware support, or skip the optional nib step.

data.name: CalibrationPolicy
data.value: Area threshold: {0:F1} DIP² · Area scale: {1:F2} · Current sensitivity: {2} (0 low / 1 medium / 2 high)

data.name: CalibrationLift
data.value: Lift all contacts before changing steps.

data.name: CalibrationInvalidOutline
data.value: Enter valid dimensions greater than 0 and no larger than 4096 DIPs.

data.name: CalibrationNeedThree
data.value: Complete at least three valid presses to continue.

data.name: CalibrationOverlap
data.value: Palm and finger samples overlap or are invalid. Go back and resample. This device may not distinguish palms by area.

data.name: CalibrationSaveFailed
data.value: Saving failed; previous settings are unchanged. Your draft is retained. Check configuration folder permissions and retry.

data.name: AvoidFullScreenHelperHint
data.value: Avoid canvas fullscreen; may fix taskbar not on top and Win11 taskbar unclickable. Can cause floating bar offset with AppBar on left/top. Restart ICC to apply.

data.name: DPIChangeDetectionHint
data.value: When a system DPI change is detected, it tries to keep FloatingBar visible. If it goes off-screen, it will attempt to move it into the visible area. (Increasing DPI may trigger this; decreasing DPI won't auto-move—adjust manually.)

data.name: EdgeGestureUtilHint_Part1
data.value: EdgeGestureUtil is newly introduced in ICC to temporarily block edge gestures when using touch (e.g., on Windows 10: swipe from the left edge to Task View, from the right edge to Action Center; on Windows 11: swipe up from the bottom to open Start). It works by using System.EdgeGesture.DisableTouchWhenFullscreen (When the app window is active and in full-screen mode (or an owned window is active), prevents edge gesture behavior.) If anything is abnormal, turn this option off; it should take effect immediately. (Not available on Windows 7/8.)

data.name: EraserBindTouchHint
data.value: BoundsWidth is used as contact area threshold

data.name: EraserBindTouchMultiplier
data.value: Bind eraser to touch size multiplier

data.name: ForceFullScreenHint
data.value: When a window size change is detected, automatically uses Win32 API to set this window size to the primary monitor size (in device pixels). Turn it off if you don't need it; takes effect immediately.

data.name: FullScreenHelperHint
data.value: Thanks to lindexi for FullScreenHelper; reduces taskbar pop-up and supports multi-monitor fullscreen. Disable if you see odd issues; restart ICC to apply.

data.name: LogLevelHint
data.value: Logs below the selected level are filtered out. Info outputs everything (no filtering); the default Trace additionally filters out the lowest-level Info/Event entries. Console colors: Info default, Trace green, Warning yellow, Error red.

data.name: LogRotateHint
data.value: When enabled, logs are saved to the Logs folder and the folder is automatically cleared when it exceeds 5 MB. Otherwise, log files exceeding 512 KB are automatically deleted.

data.name: ResolutionChangeDetectionHint
data.value: When a screen resolution change is detected, the app checks whether the FloatingBar is still within the visible screen area. If it has moved off-screen, it will try to move it back into view. This is most commonly triggered after lowering the resolution; if the FloatingBar is already visible, its position will not be adjusted automatically.

data.name: TouchMultiplierCalibrateHint
data.value: Tap with pen in the area below to estimate touch size multiplier

data.name: TouchMultiplierHint
data.value: Adjust when finger-touch shows circle eraser or palm eraser is much larger than palm

data.name: Debug_ShowConsole_Desc
data.value: Show a separate console window for live log output (takes effect immediately; if "Enable logging" is off in settings, no content will be emitted).

data.name: Debug_PPTComProbe_Desc
data.value: When enabled, outputs extensive COM object, window, process, and state probe information during PPT connection, slide show changes, and timer polling. Only enable temporarily while diagnosing PPT/WPS integration issues.

data.name: Debug_PPTPreviewVisible_Desc
data.value: When enabled, shows the inline preview area on the left side of the PPT page-flip button settings page (hidden by default).

data.name: Debug_RealtimeInkLog_Header
data.value: Enable detailed realtime ink debug log

data.name: Debug_RealtimeInkLog_Desc
data.value: When enabled, records realtime-ink input/redraw/FrameWait/slow events. Updates Configs/RealtimeInkDebugLive.json after each stroke and writes realtimeInk* fields into Configs/PerformanceHistory.json; finalizes on toggle-off or exit. Off by default; enable only while diagnosing realtime ink (TouchVelocity / realtime brush tip). Independent of the Performance page toggle. Built-in InkCanvas ink is not counted.

data.name: Debug_SimulateCrash_Desc
data.value: Click to trigger an unhandled exception immediately. Use this to verify the crash restart breaker mechanism works correctly.

data.name: Debug_SimulateHeartbeatTimeout_Desc
data.value: Click to stop the heartbeat timer. The next guard check will detect the timeout and trigger a restart.

data.name: Debug_ResetStartupCount_Desc
data.value: Clear the startup-count file to unlock the breaker lock caused by consecutive crashes.

data.name: Debug_SettingsExpanderExample_Desc
data.value: You can override the Left indention of a SettingsCard by overriding the SettingsCardLeftIndention

data.name: Debug_MemoryBreakdownDump_Header
data.value: Dump detailed memory snapshot of current process to log

data.name: Debug_MemoryBreakdownDump_Desc
data.value: Writes process memory / GC heap / WPF visuals / caches / assemblies to the Logs directory for investigation.

data.name: Debug_MemoryBreakdownForceGC_Desc
data.value: Calls GC.Collect + WaitForPendingFinalizers + GC.Collect to reclaim eligible objects. Use only for diagnostics.
